subject.title: feat(discord): add canvas-first Discord Activities support

question: Should Discord Activity support be redesigned as a Canvas-plugin/Discord-plugin feature with mandatory credentialed Activity auth, or should maintainers intentionally accept a core Gateway Activity surface with the current security and upgrade tradeoffs?
rationale: The branch crosses plugin ownership, root config, Gateway auth, token transport, runtime script loading, and WebSocket fanout boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent architecture or security contract.

options.title: Rewrite under plugin-owned contracts
options.body: Move Activity host config and routes into the Canvas plugin, keep Discord launch behavior in the Discord plugin, and require a real Activity credential or signed assertion before bypassing Gateway auth.

options.title: Accept core Gateway Activity surface
options.body: Maintain root canvasHost.activity and core Gateway auth plumbing, but explicitly own the upgrade, security, and support burden before repairing the code.

options.title: Pause until Discord Activity scope is narrower
options.body: Keep this PR open but block merge until maintainers decide whether the feature is worth carrying in core-bundled plugins now.

recommendation.title: Rewrite under plugin-owned contracts
recommendation.body: Move Activity host config and routes into the Canvas plugin, keep Discord launch behavior in the Discord plugin, and require a real Activity credential or signed assertion before bypassing Gateway auth.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main's Canvas plugin and gateway route ownership point most directly to vincentkoc for the architecture/security boundary decision.
